messages:
maria: Quick decision needed: onboarding form is long + has optional advanced blocks. Should validation be inline-as-you-type, only-on-submit, or hybrid?

dylan: Hybrid. Inline low-priority hints, but show a concise top banner on submit with count. Reduces noise while surfacing all issues.

rachel: Agree. For required markers: visible asterisk plus hidden '(required)' text for screen readers. Avoid tooltip-only explanations.

keith: Mobile: sticky submit bar with small error badge so users don't miss the banner when scrolled.

maria: Collapsed advanced sections should auto-expand on submit if they contain errors. But don't force focus into the field; keep keyboard flow predictable.

aria-bot: Accessibility checklist: aria-live region for banner (assertive on submit), invalid fields use aria-invalid + aria-describedby, dialogs trap focus.

dylan: Destructive step at end: typed-confirm for permanent deletes; modal+toast+undo for ephemeral bulk deletes (undo needs backend soft-delete).

rachel: Copy for banner: 'Fix 2 errors to continue.' Action-oriented and includes count. For typed-confirm: "Type DELETE to permanently remove 'ConfigName'."

maria: Plan: Phase 1 hybrid + sticky mobile CTA; Phase 2 auto-expand collapsed sections + anchors; Phase 3 typed-confirm + undo backend. I'll draft RFC with acceptance criteria.

dylan: I'll add figma mocks for the three banner variants and tag @design for review.
